own_scenes.place: San Francisco (Hunters Point), Oakland, Chicago y Berkeley
own_scenes.desc: El 27 de septiembre un policía mató a Matthew Johnson, de dieciséis años, en Hunters Point: disturbios, la Guardia Nacional y toque de queda en San Francisco. En Cicero, suburbio de Chicago, una turba blanca con esvásticas y carteles de «White Power» recibió a ladrillazos una marcha del SNCC. El 16 de septiembre cayó la Ley de Derechos Civiles de 1966 por un filibusterismo de Dirksen y el 52 % de los blancos creía que la integración iba «demasiado deprisa»: «white backlash» entró en el lenguaje. Carmichael, celebridad y pararrayos, llamó a rechazar el reclutamiento y el 29 de octubre, ante 8.500 personas en Berkeley, dijo que solo se pararía la guerra cuando los jóvenes dijeran «Hell, no, we ain’t going», justo lo que la campaña de Reagan necesitaba. A mediados de octubre Bobby Seale y Huey Newton redactaron en veinte minutos el programa de diez puntos del Black Panther Party, inspirados por las patrullas de vigilancia de la policía en Watts: el punto sexto, la autodefensa «por cualquier medio necesario», era la bomba de relojería.
aka: What We Want, What We Believe

refs.q: Suddenly, the phrase ‘white backlash’ entered everyday usage.
refs.para: This news compounded what had been a dreadful couple of months for the civil rights movement. It was as though some invisible line had been crossed: the movement had seen enormous gains over the last few years, but the continuing violence fuelled a wave of criticism of both the movement and President Johnson’s civil rights legislation. In the mass media the idea prevailed that things had gone too far, too fast. Suddenly, the phrase ‘white backlash’ entered everyday usage.

refs.q: It was the product of two Oakland natives, Bobby Seale and Huey Newton.
refs.para: It was the product of two Oakland natives, Bobby Seale and Huey Newton. Both were in their late twenties and both had been involved in black politics since the early sixties, most recently in the Marxist Soul Students Advisory Council. Both had had a hardscrabble upbringing marked by poverty, family violence and confrontations with authority; both had pulled themselves up by their own efforts and attended college, during which time they developed a theoretical framework to focus their anger at everyday American racism.

refs.q: Carmichael designed the speech as a major intervention on a big stage, and he succeeded.
refs.para: Carmichael designed the speech as a major intervention on a big stage, and he succeeded. As his biographer Peniel E. Joseph writes, ‘This galvanic address, carried by newspapers across the nation, made him America’s leading critic of the Vietnam War.’ It spurred on the white activists at Berkeley to resist the war in greater numbers, and gave an extra impetus to Bobby Seale and Huey Newton to put their programme in action and organise the Black Panthers as a viable, radical Black Power group.
